core_obligations: The transfinite construction (proof lines 1864-1888): starting from the zero subcomplex, the author builds an increasing ordinal-indexed family of acyclic subcomplexes of an arbitrary acyclic complex, inserting at successor steps a subcomplex of bounded size inside a nonzero acyclic quotient and taking colimits at limit ordinals, and notes that the family exhausts the complex for a large enough ordinal.

Successor steps (proof lines 1889-1903): the vanishing of morphisms from the constructed subcomplex into the given complex is propagated from an ordinal to its successor by the long exact sequence for the two short exact sequences attached to the construction, using the injectivity of the terms and the hypothesis on bounded above acyclic complexes.

Limit ordinals (proof lines 1903-1918): at a limit ordinal the complex of morphisms is the limit of the earlier ones, the transition maps are surjective because the terms of the target are injective, and the Mittag-Leffler lemma for ordinals is applied, which gives the vanishing there; since the family exhausts the complex, the criterion follows.
proof_roadmap: Build an ordinal-indexed increasing family of acyclic subcomplexes exhausting an arbitrary acyclic complex.
Propagate the vanishing of morphisms through successor ordinals using the short exact sequences and injectivity.
Handle limit ordinals by identifying the complex of morphisms with a limit and applying the Mittag-Leffler lemma.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a criterion for a complex with injective terms to be K-injective, namely the vanishing of homotopy classes of maps from every bounded above acyclic complex of bounded cardinality (statement lines 1849-1862). The proof is a complete transfinite induction: an ordinal-indexed family of acyclic subcomplexes exhausting an arbitrary acyclic complex is constructed (proof lines 1864-1888); the vanishing of morphisms is propagated through successor ordinals using the two short exact sequences and the injectivity of the terms together with the hypothesis (proof lines 1889-1903); and at limit ordinals the complex of morphisms is identified with a limit whose transition maps are surjective, so that the Mittag-Leffler lemma for ordinals applies (proof lines 1903-1918). The non-formal content is the transfinite construction and its limit analysis. The claim is H3.
